chunks: And from him, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Amr, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who accumulates for him from the zakat five hundred and six hundred [coins], and he buys from it a slave whom he manumissions. He said, 'Then he wrongs other people regarding their rights.' Then he paused for a while, then said, 'Unless it is a Muslim slave in need, then let him buy him and manumiss him.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And there is no objection to preferring the relatives over others, up to his saying: And there is no objection to giving the zakat to the children of the believers.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use accumulated zakat funds to buy and free a single slave?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that concentrating zakat on a single slave for manumission constitutes injustice to the broader community of recipients, unless the slave is in dire necessity. This ruling is contextualized by Shaykh al-Tusi’s note on the permissibility of preferring kin and children of believers, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing communal equity with familial solidarity. The discussion highlights the jurisprudential nuance between general distribution and specific, need-based exceptions within the eight categories of zakat recipients.
